story.title: Jensen Huang to Testify Before Congress on Nvidia's National Security Concerns
story.summary: Jensen Huang, former CEO of Nvidia, has agreed to testify before several congressional committees on December 1 regarding the company's sales to China and potential national security risks. This hearing follows his resignation amid allegations of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia has also established a national security committee in response to these issues.

Following the announcement of the investigation, Nvidia's stock price experienced a significant drop, and US intelligence officials have raised concerns about the implications of this relationship.

event_overview.title: About Corporate Espionage
event_overview.subject: Corporate Espionage
event_overview.summary: Corporate espionage is the unlawful acquisition or attempted acquisition of a company’s nonpublic commercial or technical information for competitive, commercial, or state benefit. In the United States, allegations involving a foreign government or agent may fall within the distinct federal offense of economic espionage; allegations alone do not establish that trade secrets were obtained, that a foreign nexus existed, or that a crime occurred.

facts.label: Definition
facts.value: The FBI describes economic espionage as foreign power-sponsored or coordinated intelligence activity aimed at unlawfully obtaining sensitive economic, proprietary, or critical-technology information, or unlawfully influencing sensitive economic-policy decisions.

facts.label: Federal legal framework
facts.value: The Economic Espionage Act of 1996 created the core federal trade-secret offenses in Chapter 90 of Title 18, including economic espionage (§1831) and theft of trade secrets (§1832).

facts.label: Foreign-government nexus
facts.value: Section 1831 applies when a person knowingly steals, receives, transmits, attempts to obtain, or conspires to obtain a trade secret while intending or knowing that the offense will benefit a foreign government, foreign instrumentality, or foreign agent.

facts.label: Related commercial offense
facts.value: Section 1832 separately criminalizes knowingly taking or receiving a trade secret related to interstate or foreign commerce for another’s economic benefit, with intent or knowledge that the owner will be injured; it does not require proof of a foreign-government beneficiary.

facts.label: Investigation and prosecution
facts.value: The FBI investigates suspected economic espionage and trade-secret theft, while the Justice Department directs prosecutors to prioritize such matters, especially theft involving advanced technology, critical infrastructure, national-security interests, or foreign transfer.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline tracks the reported Nvidia-related allegations, corporate response, leadership developments, and congressional attention from November 9–17, 2026; it does not by itself establish the facts of the allegations, determine criminal liability, or provide a complete record of any government or internal investigation.

explore_lenses.label: What will happen in Congress on December 1?
explore_lenses.title: A closed, transcribed interview—not a public hearing
explore_lenses.summary: Huang has agreed to a voluntary transcribed interview with three House committees on December 1. Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear separately on December 2.

claims.text: The House Intelligence, Foreign Affairs, and Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party said Huang and Teter agreed to appear voluntarily; Huang’s interview is set for December 1 and Teter’s for December 2.

The committees’ original November 4 request sought a joint closed-door briefing about Nvidia’s anti-espionage protocols and Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang; it requested an appearance on November 18 or an alternative date.

Chairmen Rick Crawford, Brian Mast, and John Moolenaar say they want answers about possible access by PRC actors to advanced chips and the alleged role of a Chinese intelligence asset; this is the committees’ stated rationale, not a congressional finding.

explore_lenses.label: Why are Nvidia’s China sales central to the inquiry?
explore_lenses.title: The dispute centers on export-control screening
explore_lenses.summary: The congressional inquiry joins a broader dispute over how the government screens advanced-chip sales to China and guards against diversion. The official export policy permits case-by-case review for some Nvidia H200 exports, subject to stated security conditions.

claims.text: The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security said in January that H200 and comparable-chip export-license applications to China would be reviewed case by case, provided applicants meet conditions including customer screening, U.S. testing, and assurances that exports will not reduce capacity available to U.S. customers.
BIS says advanced-computing chips can support military-intelligence and weapons-related uses and has warned industry about illegal diversion schemes involving such chips.
Mast, Moolenaar, and Crawford argue that Congress must determine whether PRC access to sensitive U.S. technology and information put national security at risk.

Sen. Ron Wyden and Rep. Richard Neal, the ranking members of the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means Committees, have requested preservation of Commerce records and argue that its licensing process may have lacked adequate due diligence; those are lawmakers’ allegations, not adjudicated findings.

explore_lenses.label: What changed at Nvidia after Huang resigned?
explore_lenses.title: Colette Kress is interim CEO
explore_lenses.summary: Huang’s departure formally changed Nvidia’s leadership, with CFO Colette Kress taking the interim CEO role while the board searches for a permanent successor. The company’s official announcement does not document the reported creation of a separate national-security committee.

claims.text: Nvidia’s board accepted Jen-Hsun Huang’s resignation as president, CEO, and a board member effective immediately; its November 12 SEC filing says Kress was appointed interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent chief executive.
The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones as chair; he has served on Nvidia’s board since 1993, according to the company’s SEC filing.
Nvidia’s board says it expects operations, customer commitments, and the product roadmap to continue without interruption; this is a company forecast.
Neither Nvidia’s November 12 newsroom announcement nor its related SEC filing mentions a newly formed national-security committee.

story_report.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is set to appear voluntarily before House committees on Dec. 1 for questioning over the company’s sales to China and potential national-security risks. The appearance follows Huang’s resignation after allegations involving a suspected Chinese intelligence asset; Nvidia’s board appointed Colette Kress interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor. The congressional inquiry is expected to examine safeguards around sensitive technology and Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang.

sections.heading: House committees schedule Nvidia interviews
sections.body: The House Intelligence, Foreign Affairs and Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party said Huang and Nvidia executive Teter agreed to appear voluntarily. Huang’s interview is scheduled for Dec. 1 and Teter’s for Dec. 2. In a Nov. 4 request, the committees sought a joint closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s anti-espionage protocols and Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang.

sections.heading: Export rules govern advanced chips
sections.body: The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security said in January that export-license applications to China for Nvidia’s H200 and comparable chips would be considered case by case. Applicants must meet conditions including customer screening, U.S. testing and assurances that exports will not reduce supply available to U.S. customers. BIS has said advanced-computing chips can support military-intelligence and weapons-related uses, and has warned companies about illegal diversion schemes.

sections.heading: Nvidia board installs interim leadership
sections.body: Nvidia’s board accepted Jen-Hsun Huang’s resignation as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately, according to its SEC filing. The board named Kress interim CEO and appointed longtime director Harvey C. Jones as chair. Nvidia has said it expects operations, customer commitments and its product roadmap to continue without interruption, a company forecast rather than an established outcome.

unresolved.text: The available official materials do not establish that Nvidia or Huang violated export-control law, and they do not resolve allegations involving Alice Huang or Megaspeed.
The House announcement does not say whether interview transcripts will be made public or what documents Huang and Nvidia will provide.
Official Nvidia and SEC materials reviewed do not substantiate the reported formation of a national-security committee.

Trump has issued a warning to Iran regarding these allegations.
